title: Design a Vector Database / ANN Search Service
prompt: Design a vector database that stores billions of embeddings and serves approximate nearest-neighbor search with metadata filtering. It must offer tunable recall/latency, support inserts/updates/deletes without full rebuilds, scale across shards, and back workloads like semantic search and RAG retrieval.
blurb: The ANN engine — HNSW vs IVF, sharding and replication, filtered search, the recall/latency/memory tradeoff, and live updates.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (upsert, kNN query, metadata filter, delete) from non-functional (recall target, query latency, insert throughput, freshness, durability).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about vector count and dimension, distance metric, target recall, latency budget, update rate, filtering needs, and multi-tenancy.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Estimates raw vector storage (N x dim x 4B), index memory overhead (HNSW graph, IVF lists), query QPS, and per-shard fanout — deciding what fits in RAM vs needs quantization.

rubric.label: Index algorithm choice
rubric.description: HNSW vs IVF(-PQ) vs flat; graph vs cluster tradeoffs; build cost, memory, recall/latency, and when each wins.

rubric.label: Recall/latency/memory tradeoff
rubric.description: Tuning ef/nprobe, quantization (PQ/SQ) vs recall, and how to measure and hit a recall target within a latency budget.

rubric.label: Filtered search
rubric.description: Combining metadata predicates with ANN — pre-filter vs post-filter vs filtered-graph traversal, and the recall collapse of naive post-filtering under selective filters.

rubric.label: Sharding & replication
rubric.description: Partitioning vectors across shards, scatter-gather query with top-k merge, replication for QPS and HA, and rebalancing.

rubric.label: Updates & deletes
rubric.description: Incremental inserts into graph/list indexes, tombstoning deletes, handling index degradation, and background compaction/rebuild.

rubric.label: Freshness & sync
rubric.description: Bounded staleness between write and searchable, and keeping vectors in sync when upstream source data changes.

rubric.label: ML/embedding specifics
rubric.description: Embedding dimension and metric choice, normalization, handling an embedding-model change (reindex), and quantization impact on recall.

rubric.label: Scaling & performance
rubric.description: In-memory vs on-disk (DiskANN-style) indexes, caching hot vectors, batching queries, and horizontal scale.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Recall sampling against exact kNN, p99 latency, index build/compaction lag, memory pressure, and per-shard skew.

functional_requirements: Upsert vectors with metadata (id, embedding, attributes)
kNN / ANN query returning top-k by distance (cosine/dot/L2)
Metadata-filtered search (e.g. tenant, tag, date range)
nonfunctional_requirements: Tunable recall (e.g. 95%+ recall@10) within a p99 latency budget (~tens of ms)
High insert throughput without blocking queries
Bounded freshness: newly inserted vectors searchable within seconds
Durability of vectors and metadata; index rebuildable from source
Horizontal scale to billions of vectors
clarifying_questions: How many vectors and what dimension? Distance metric?
Target recall and p99 latency budget?
Insert/update/delete rate — mostly static or streaming?
How selective are metadata filters, and are they high-cardinality?
Single-tenant or many namespaces? Memory budget / cost target?
Is exact kNN ever required, or is approximate always acceptable?
qualifying_questions: Do we need in-memory latency or is disk-backed acceptable for cost?
Will the embedding model change over time (forcing reindex)?

estimations.raw_storage: 1B vectors x 768 dims x 4B ≈ 3TB raw; sharded across nodes
estimations.index_memory: HNSW adds graph links (M neighbors x ~8B x N) — often 1.5-2x raw; ~4.5-6TB in RAM for 1B unless quantized
estimations.quantized: PQ/SQ can cut memory ~4-16x (e.g. 3TB → ~200-750GB) at some recall cost — enables fewer nodes or disk
estimations.qps_fanout: A scatter-gather query hits every shard; with S shards, one logical query = S index searches + a top-k merge
estimations.build_cost: HNSW build is O(N log N) graph insertions — hours for billions; IVF training samples a subset to learn centroids

core_components: Ingest / write path (validate, assign shard, buffer)
Index engine per shard (HNSW / IVF-PQ / flat)
Metadata store + attribute index for filtering
Replication + durability (WAL, snapshots to object store)
data_model: vectors(id PK, namespace, embedding[dim], shard_id, created_at, version)
metadata(id FK, attrs jsonb / columnar, tombstoned bool)
wal(seq, op, id, payload) — for durability/replay
api_design: POST /collections/{ns}/query { vector, k, filter?, ef?/nprobe? } → { matches:[{id, score, metadata}] }
POST /collections { name, dim, metric, index_params } → { ok }
reference.high_level_design: Writes go to a coordinator that routes by id/namespace to a shard, appends to a WAL for durability, and inserts into the shard's in-memory index (HNSW graph or IVF list) while updating the metadata store; deletes tombstone the id. Queries: coordinator scatters the query vector to all shards (or a routed subset), each shard runs ANN with a tuned search parameter (ef for HNSW, nprobe for IVF), applies the metadata filter during traversal, returns local top-k; the coordinator merges to global top-k and optionally reranks with full-precision distances. A background worker compacts segments, purges tombstones, and rebuilds degraded indexes. Snapshots persist to object storage so any node can rebuild. Recall is monitored by periodically running exact kNN on a sample and comparing.

deep_dives.probe: HNSW vs IVF-PQ for 1B vectors — compare memory, build time, recall/latency, and update-friendliness. When would you pick each?

A query filters to a tenant that's 0.1% of vectors. Naive post-filtering after ANN returns almost nothing. How do you do filtered ANN correctly — pre-filter, filtered graph traversal, or partitioned indexes?
You need recall@10 ≥ 95% at p99 < 20ms. Which knobs (ef/nprobe, M, PQ codebook size) do you turn, and how do you measure recall in production without ground truth?
HNSW doesn't love deletes. How do you handle high update/delete churn without full rebuilds — tombstones, segment compaction, periodic rebuild?
How do you shard billions of vectors and merge top-k across shards? What about skew and rebalancing when one namespace grows huge?
You can't fit the raw vectors in RAM. Walk me through PQ/scalar quantization, the recall hit, and rerank-with-full-precision to recover it.

followup_bank.trigger: mentions embeddings or embedding model or source data
followup_bank.question: When the upstream source that produced an embedding changes, how does the vector stay in sync — CDC from the source re-embedding only changed items, versioning, tombstoning the old vector? And if you swap embedding models, how do you reindex billions without downtime?
What do you cache — hot query results or hot vectors/segments — and what's the eviction policy? How do you invalidate cached results after an upsert/delete so you don't serve stale neighbors?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or metadata store or postgres
followup_bank.question: How do you keep the vector index and the metadata store consistent on writes — CDC vs transactional dual-write vs WAL replay?
How do you rebuild a shard's index online without dropping queries or blocking writes?

scaling: Shard by id/namespace; scatter-gather with global top-k merge
Replicas per shard for QPS and HA; route reads to least-loaded replica
Disk-backed indexes (DiskANN-style) + SSD for cost when RAM-bound
Quantization to shrink memory footprint per node
Batch/vectorized query execution and hot-vector caching
bottlenecks: Memory: index overhead often exceeds raw vector size
Filtered search recall collapse with selective/high-cardinality filters
Index degradation and rebuild cost under heavy deletes
Recall/latency/memory is a hard three-way tradeoff
tradeoffs: HNSW (great recall/latency, high memory, update-friendly-ish) vs IVF-PQ (cheaper memory, needs training, coarser)
More shards (parallelism) vs merge overhead and tail latency
alternative_solutions: Flat/brute-force exact search for small collections
ScaNN / DiskANN for disk-scale or anisotropic quantization
Embed vectors in an existing OLTP/OLAP store with a vector extension (simpler ops, less specialized)
observability: Sampled recall vs exact kNN ground truth
p50/p99 query latency and per-shard latency skew
Index build/compaction lag and tombstone ratio
Memory pressure and segment counts per shard
Insert throughput and freshness lag (write → searchable)
security: Namespace/tenant isolation of indexes and queries
Auth + per-namespace access control on query and upsert
Rate limiting to protect shared nodes
Audit of who queried/modified which namespace
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer clarifies vector count, dimension, metric, target recall, and latency, then estimates raw storage vs index memory overhead to decide in-memory vs quantized vs disk. It picks an index (HNSW for recall/latency and updates, IVF-PQ for memory-constrained billions) with explicit reasoning, and tunes ef/nprobe and quantization against a measured recall target — sampling exact kNN in production to track recall without labels. It handles filtered search correctly (pre-filter or filtered traversal, not naive post-filter that collapses recall on selective filters), shards with scatter-gather + top-k merge and replicas for QPS/HA, and manages updates/deletes via tombstones + background compaction/rebuild rather than blocking rebuilds. It addresses freshness and embedding-model-change reindexing, and names the recall/latency/memory three-way tradeoff, filtered-search recall, and scatter-gather tail latency as the key bottlenecks.

interviewer_notes: The differentiator here is whether the candidate reasons about the recall/latency/memory tradeoff quantitatively and knows why index overhead can exceed raw vector size. Push the index-algorithm deep dive (HNSW vs IVF-PQ) and don't accept 'just use HNSW' without the memory and update caveats. The filtered-search probe is the sharpest signal — many candidates naively post-filter after ANN and don't realize recall collapses under selective filters; make them get to pre-filtering or filtered traversal. Use the embedding-sync follow-up (CDC re-embed on source change, reindex on model swap) and the cache-invalidation follow-up as interrupts. Ask how they measure recall in prod without ground truth — sampling exact kNN is the expected answer. Reserve time for updates/deletes and online rebuild; a candidate who only designs a static index is missing the hard part.
